dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: indrajālamayaṃ viśvaṃ vyastaṃ vā citrakarmavat | bhramad vā dhyāyataḥ sarvam paśyataś ca sukhodgamaḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: For one who contemplates the whole universe as a magic show, or as scattered like the figures of a painting, or as whirling, and who sees everything in this way, happiness arises.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the cosmos is seen as jugglery conjured by a magician, as the configuration of a painting, or as illusory as the apparent movement of trees seen from a moving boat; Jayaratha cites this verse too as an example of sarvātma-saṃkoca. Wallis: a magic show, a wondrous painting, or constantly in flux.
dharana.technique_name: The World as a Magic Show or a Painting
dharana.instruction: Look at the world around you as a vivid magic show or painting, and notice the lightness that comes.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 79' = verse 102 (agrees with Singh)
The Mystery Within (2019), parallel translations: 'Dharana 79 • verso 102' (agrees)
Wallis concordance: verse 102 = 'Like a painting (Y77 ~ B1)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 102 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 102 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: seen as a magic show, a painting, or a moving scene
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the world around you seen as a display, vivid but not solid, like a painting or a conjured scene.
geometry.svg_hint: a framed scene drawn in light strokes, slightly shimmering
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: See it as a display
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a world that feels heavy and solid is seen as a vivid display, and the heart lightens. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The world seen as a magic show, a painting, or a scene in constant motion
attention.secondary: The happiness that comes with that lightness

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: For one who contemplates the whole universe as a magic show, or as scattered like the figures of a painting, or as whirling, and who sees everything in this way, happiness arises.
adiyogi.method_summary: Look around, or recall the day, and see it as a magic show, a painting, or a scene passing from a moving boat: vivid, but not solid. Hold that view gently and notice the lightness and happiness that arise.

honesty.disclosure: Door 079 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 79 (verse 102) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 079 is dharana 79, verse 102. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Seeing the world as a display does not mean other people's pain is unreal; keep care and responsibility in view. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
